BERT4Rec predicts from an appended reserved mask token’s hidden state ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690)). Recommended export checks: compare checkpoint and exported scores in evaluation mode; verify left-padding, truncation that reserves mask space, and final nonpadding readout. Test candidate permutation equivariance, singleton/batched scoring parity, and category-request order independence. Avoid assuming padding-shift invariance when absolute positions change.

Inject four isolated internal mutations, leaving test oracles untouched: replace final-position gathering with `nonpadding_count-1`; omit mask insertion while retaining valid tensor shapes; swap two valid candidate-to-embedding mappings only; redirect one category to another checkpoint. Independently establish applicability through execution traces or hooks: a padded fixture yields different readout indices; encoded input actually loses its mask; selected distinct IDs reach swapped embedding rows; routing loads the wrong checkpoint identity using shape-compatible fixtures. Establish activation before checking detection. Report applicable/killed/surviving/inapplicable separately; crashes are interface failures, not evidence that semantic assertions detected the fault. Unchanged HR@10 alone does not establish equivalence.

For simulator recommendations, score the entire category catalog with its single model; exclude every item in the supplied observed history, including truncated-away interactions, plus padding/mask IDs. Filter before selection and return fewer than k when insufficient eligible items remain. Compare dense scoring against multiple chunk sizes and traversal orders, merging chunk-local top-k under the same total order. Use descending score, then ascending canonical item ID; include ties across chunk boundaries. PyTorch warns that [`topk` ties are unstable](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html); ID presorting followed by [stable score sorting](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.argsort.html) implements the proposed order. Check score tolerance and exact ranked-ID parity separately. Keep these simulator checks separate from—and do not change—the pinned benchmark’s candidate filtering or tie semantics.
